public_rationale: The available records complicate the broad claim: Stanford reports substantial investment outside the generative-AI category, and DARPA documents a funded alternative approach. But neither source measures the relevant US LLM-versus-alternative investment share. The categories, coverage, and undefined threshold prevent a fair supported or contradicted verdict.
limitations: The observation period is an explicit annual-reporting interpretation.
Generative AI and LLMs are not interchangeable investment categories.
Budget entries are not proof of actual expenditure.
The DARPA document's availability date is a conservative month-end bound.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Very little investment has gone into AI approaches other than LLMs.

statement.excerpt: Meanwhile, precious little investment has been made in other approaches.
statement.document_title: CONFIRMED: LLMs have indeed reached a point of diminishing returns

our_interpretation: The plain contextual reading is that alternative AI approaches received a small share of investment compared with LLM approaches, especially in the United States.
The adjacent references to trustworthy AI and US policy suggest alternatives to relying on LLM scaling, rather than every application outside language generation.

For the ongoing, unperiodized investment comparison, use calendar 2023 as the latest complete annual investment reporting period available before the post. This does not establish the position during all of 2024.
No numerical meaning of 'precious little' is supplied, so no arbitrary percentage cutoff is imposed.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable investment records show that alternative approaches received only a small share relative to LLM approaches under a consistent classification.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records show a substantial share directed to alternative approaches, under the same geographic and investment coverage.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A consistent investment breakdown for the relevant geography and period, separating LLM approaches from alternative architectures and distinguishing financing from expenditure, with a defensible interpretation of 'precious little.'
